title: Dev-loop latency: concurrent xtask test preflights
head: b6184e71

host.note: Load was not held at a fixed level. Both arms were measured with frozen harness binaries in interleaved rounds, so drift applies to both arms; the arm ranges do not overlap.

lever.name: run the three `xtask test` preflights concurrently
lever.payload: 4 tests, 0.00 s of test execution, no rebuild
lever.harness: two frozen `xtask` binaries built from the same HEAD, one with the preflights serial (`before`) and one with them concurrent (`after`); cargo is never invoked to rebuild the harness inside the timed window

gate_components.note: Run one after another in the order above. The concurrent gate costs the slowest of the three, i.e. max(latencies), not their sum.

contract_bucket_counts.note: The 23 failures are the loud feature guard: CI passes `--features perimeter-spatial-test-support`. They are not a red tree.

falsified.premise: `cargo check` and `cargo clippy` do not share artifacts, so alternating between them re-checks the workspace.
falsified.measurement: After both were warm, an alternation in either direction took 1.7-2.4 s and reported 0 `Checking` lines. The earlier 129-138 s readings came from a dirty `slicer-runtime` test target left by a reverted probe edit, not from an artifact split.

falsified.premise: Feature-set divergence (`slicer-core/host-algos` injected by `xtask test`, absent from the documented narrow command) forces a full rebuild when an agent switches commands.
falsified.measurement: A plain `cargo test -p slicer-runtime --test contract ... --no-run` immediately after a host-algos `xtask test` run finished in 0.72 s with no rebuild.
falsified.verdict: dead for `slicer-runtime` (it already enables the feature); the injected feature still breaks packages that do not depend on `slicer-core` — see adjacent_findings

falsified.premise: The linker is a large share of the local loop, so lld/mold would buy a big win.
falsified.measurement: A relink-only step (binary and PDB deleted, incremental objects warm) took 12.8 s; the dominant cost is codegen, not linking. Not measured on a cold full build.
falsified.verdict: dead for incremental relinks; cold-build link share unmeasured

falsified.premise: Dropping debug info speeds the rebuild an agent pays.
falsified.measurement: The same incremental contract rebuild took 17.3 s at the default `debug = 2` and 28.2 s with `profile.test.package.slicer-runtime.debug = 0`.
falsified.verdict: not a win on the incremental path; cold-build effect unmeasured

adjacent_findings.finding: `cargo xtask test -p <package>` fails for any package that does not depend on `slicer-core`.
adjacent_findings.reproduction: cargo xtask test -p xtask --summary -> error: the package 'xtask' does not contain this feature: slicer-core/host-algos
adjacent_findings.cause: `test_command` appends `--features slicer-core/host-algos` unless the caller set features, without checking whether the selected package resolves that dependency feature.
adjacent_findings.impact: the documented gated entry point cannot run `-p xtask`, `-p slicer-config`, `-p slicer-ir`, `-p slicer-scheduler`, `-p slicer-gcode`, or `-p slicer-helpers`

adjacent_findings.finding: The documented narrow command's test filter matches no test.
adjacent_findings.reproduction: cargo test -p slicer-runtime --test contract core_module_ir_access_contract_tdd -> 0 passed; 314 filtered out
adjacent_findings.cause: AGENTS.md carries `core_module_ir_access_contract_tdd` as the example filter; the contract bucket no longer contains a test by that name.
adjacent_findings.impact: the documented narrow command builds the bucket and runs nothing, which reads as green

ruled_out.lever: blaze (formerly ra-jit) — rust-analyzer + Cranelift incremental build daemon
ruled_out.reason: Upstream states it supports macOS on Apple silicon and Linux only: 'Windows has no installer, and v2 has not been run there.' This take's measured host is x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, so the tool cannot change any build or test wall reported here. It is not a priced-and-rejected lever.
ruled_out.ci_note: The repository's CI runs ubuntu-latest, where the tool exists, but it ships its own pinned Rust nightly and upstream itself says 'your toolchain and CI stay the final word'. It could not act as the gate compiler for a repo pinned to 1.96.0 with a controlled-perimeter accelerated build; that is reasoning from the vendor docs, not a measurement.

not_priced: cold-workspace build effect of `debug = 1` / `debug = 0` (needs two clean target dirs)
linker substitution on a cold full build
cargo-nextest execution advantage on the five test buckets
sccache and CI-side caching / job-graph changes (no CI runner available locally)
